title: Reuse and extend behavior with inheritance
goal: Create a subclass that reuses a superclass method and adds its own behavior with super.
paragraphs: A subclass is defined with < followed by its superclass name. It can use the superclass methods and define its own methods. A method with the same name overrides the inherited method for instances of the subclass.

Here, super continues lookup at the next matching method; for Alert#label, that is Message#label. Bare super forwards the arguments received by the current method. In Alert#initialize, bare super would pass both text and level to Message#initialize, which accepts only text. super(text) passes just the argument Message#initialize expects. In label, bare super works because label receives no arguments.
code:
class Message
  def initialize(text)
    @text = text
  end

  def label
    "Message: #{@text}"
  end
end

class Alert < Message
  def initialize(text, level)
    super(text)
    @level = level
  end

  def label
    "#{super} (#{@level})"
  end
end

puts Alert.new("Check the door", "urgent").label
pitfall: Defining Alert#label overrides the inherited label for Alert objects. If the override never calls super, the Message label is not included.
remaining: Multiple inheritance is not supported by classes; module mix-ins are a separate mechanism.

experiments.title: Add a prefix
experiments.task: Change Alert#label so the output begins with "ALERT: ", while keeping the message and level. Which call lets the subclass keep the superclass label?
experiments.answer: Add "ALERT: " before super in Alert#label, for example "ALERT: #{super} (#{@level})". The output becomes ALERT: Message: Check the door (urgent). Here, super continues lookup to Message#label, the next matching implementation, so Alert can add text without copying that method.

class Alert < Message

  end
end

puts Alert.new("Check the door", "urgent").label

experiments.title: Change the level
experiments.task: Change the level to info. Which part of the output changes?
experiments.answer: The superclass message stays the same; the subclass appends (info).
